title: Sticks, bass drum size, muting and tuning, drumheads
summary: He gives views on sticks, his 14x26 bass drum, muting, tuning, weather, and a broken head at a parade.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: I was going to ask if you like heavy sticks or light sticks?
I like sticks, no, sort of a medium size, yeah, for dance band, medium size. Not too heavy, not too light.
And what about the bass drum? Do you like a bigger bass drum or smaller or the tone doesn't make much difference in the tone?

My idea, the bass drum I'm working on now is a 1426. And I had that drum now since 1950 I've got that drum. And it's, I think it's, my idea about it is it's got a better tone than a smaller size bass, you know, for a lot of jazz band. But I don't know, I can't take it to the smaller size bass, you know, the modern style.
I don't like it, it looks like a little tom-tom.

Little tom-toms, yeah. Really? But I really like the bass drum I'm working on now. I think that's a 1426 bass. And I believe that's, my idea is best for jazz, better volume. And then you take this kind of damp weather right now, that instrument will still, you just give it a certain tune-up, it'll hold its volume, you know. And the way I pad, man, mute it. Now I just have a side muffler to it, and I take some old pieces of these, what you call this, these pads you put on your back, you know, for pains like that, these plastic pads. And I make that in a round shape, I figure it's the biggest ashtray, for the ball to hit it, get it. And I notice that gives it a better tone in my mute. You see, some guys mute the drummer, but I just, I don't ever mute my, I was learned, it was told by old drummers, when they first started muting drums, don't mute the back part of a drum, always mute the side where your ball hit it. Some guys used to use it.

a piece of rag over it, well that makes the drum too tudd like, you understand? It's like your snare. Now the good drum like Contra, they all explain it, tune your snare drum, maybe a twist more on the batter side and let the snare side a little looser. It gives it a better volume too.
Do you try to tune up your drums to any certain pitch like on the piano or on another

instrument? I did it years ago, tried to reach it, yeah, years ago I used to do it when I worked with Pilon band and we tried it, we did it awhile, you know. Sometimes it'll hold up, sometimes it wouldn't. Sometimes the weather, the way a drum will, see like you get into a heated place like in the wintertime, the drum with the heat, you understand it'll draw off the head, you can sometimes pop it. Or you might get a rain, you take the summer night, you can have winter weather, you get a rain like out there now, that could interfere with the snare drum most of the time too. That'll give you trouble around this part of the world.
Have much trouble breaking heads on your snare drum ever?

Not too much, no. Last drum head I had broke was the Sunday we played, I played with the Eureka Brass Band, we had a rain and I was a drummer, yeah, couldn't help that Sunday, that's quite a while back, head broke on me.
Did it get soft and your stick went through it or?

No, it just rim cut, in fact I was covering it all the time, you know, this wiping, we were making different little stops. But before the parade was over there, she rim cut on me from the dampness, you see. And I had to unwind it, in fact she just had it there, couldn't do nothing with it, because you tried to play it, you couldn't sound like nothing, you see. But we just had to finish the parade, and the band, when the drums get wet, they don't look, you know the band, they expect to hear those drums, they know they don't sound like nothing, you can't play it. Now they did, they tell me they got covers to put on the drum.
They say you ought to try to sell those plastic covers.
That's what they tell me, they tell me they got all that now.
You can get a piece of plastic back from the cleaners, from, you know, in the way I had.
Yeah, that would take it, yeah.
Help it a whole lot, help a snare drum out, yeah.
